assumptions: A1. Locally defined synthetic credentials can sign in to demonstrate reset and session invalidation; no additional password policy, production identity provider, persistent account store or particular post-sign-in UX is specified.
A2. The reset-request identifier is an email; reset pages are simply server-rendered, with exact appearance and error copy unspecified.

A3. Links for eligible known synthetic accounts and successful-reset notifications are observable through an in-memory sink for authorized local demonstration and tests; no real email is sent and no public reset response contains a link.

A4. The five-per-account-per-hour limit is interpreted as a rolling hour for known synthetic accounts; no numeric quota for nonexistent accounts is inferred and their public response remains indistinguishable.
A5. An unused link is usable before 30 minutes from issuance and invalid at or after that boundary; the boundary convention is an interpretation, not a literal quote from ACC-STD-02.

Only a static sign-in wireframe is supplied. No live app, interaction, reset-page design, accessibility evaluation, runtime behavior or test result is evidenced; the approved requirements were read under requirements_analysis without a returned source locator, so no stage_output citation is asserted.

open_questions.question: What exact layout and copy should the unpictured recovery, error, success and authenticated screens use?
open_questions.context: Only the sign-in screen is pictured; proposed screen structure is not a visual observation.

open_questions.question: What password rules, if any, and what minimal sign-in success UX should be chosen?
open_questions.context: A1 does not authorize inventing an additional password policy or a production identity integration.

open_questions.question: Should invalid, used and expired links share one neutral error message, or vary without disclosing a token or account?
open_questions.context: The standard requires single use and issuance-based expiry but does not dictate public error wording.

open_questions.question: How will authorized local demonstrators inspect the in-memory sink without placing links or notifications on public pages?
open_questions.context: A3 requires private local observability, not a public recovery-link display.

open_questions.question: What validation copy and perceptible submission-progress treatment are suitable for the server-rendered forms?
open_questions.context: Keep known, unknown and rate-limited reset-request responses identical after valid submission.

findings.statement: The static sign-in wireframe shows a white page with a centered, thin dark-outlined rectangular card and a prominent bold “Sign in” heading; it does not establish rendered behavior.
The pictured card has an “Email address” label and input displaying the `name@example.com` placeholder.
The pictured card has a “Password” label and input displaying masked-looking `********` placeholder characters; actual typed-character masking is not observable.
A blue underlined “Forgot password?” link is pictured below the password input; its destination is not observable in the static image.
The card shows a wide dark “Sign in” button, without evidence of submission behavior.
The sign-in view shows the footer “No account? Contact your administrator.”

Make the pictured password field actually mask typed characters, preserve its visible placeholder and label, and make the sign-in controls keyboard-operable with visible focus, associated labels and clear accessible validation; none of these interaction properties is demonstrated by the image.

Following “Forgot password?” should open a server-rendered reset-request form with a labeled email field, submit action and sign-in return route; the pictured link alone does not prove this destination.

Submitting valid local synthetic credentials should reach a minimal authenticated result backed by an active session; sign-in error, empty fields and progress should be understandable without displaying a password. The result and session are unpictured.

After a syntactically valid reset request, show the same public acknowledgement and response outcome for known, unknown and rate-limited identifiers; disclose neither existence nor link. For eligible known synthetic accounts, record a usable link only in the local in-memory sink; a sixth request within a rolling hour issues no further link, without changing the public UI.

Opening an unused link before 30 minutes since issuance should present a server-rendered new-password form with masked labeled input and accessible validation; successful submission updates the password and consumes that link once. A token that is invalid, already used or at/after the 30-minute boundary should instead reach a neutral error state with a fresh-request path, without changing the password or exposing token/account details.

A successful reset should show a neutral confirmation and sign-in route, never the new password or a link. Completion invalidates every previous session and records an owner notification after each success in the local in-memory sink, not in a public notification page or external email; the confirmation itself cannot prove those effects.
